content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) outlines various insulin plans, each with specific characteristics and considerations. Injected insulin plans provide flexibility in dosing but are associated with an increased risk of hypoglycemia. These plans typically require multiple daily injections to manage blood glucose levels effectively. Multi-Dose Injections (MDI) involve the use of long-acting basal insulin to maintain a steady background level of insulin throughout the day, combined with rapid-acting or ultra-rapid-acting insulin administered before meals to manage postprandial glucose spikes. NPH-based plans incorporate injections of regular or short-acting insulin alongside NPH (Neutral Protamine Hagedorn) insulin. These plans are suitable for individuals who may benefit from a less intensive insulin regimen while still achieving adequate glycemic control.
